_doc: The gate in BUILDING_EXPANSION.md §9: you do not start with a ship and you cannot buy one. Four subsystems — hull, drive, tanks, avionics — each built from a DIFFERENT refined material so the whole of the refining chain gets used, one of them (the drive) needing a rare element off the planet you are standing on, fuel that is a separate consumable, and a launch pad you place like any other structure. Read by js/shipyard.js. Every id here comes from data/workshop.json; every element key comes from universe/data/elements.json.
_balanceDoc: §9.20 asks for the whole gate to be one tunable block in data/balance.json. That file belongs to another pair of hands this round, so the block lives here instead and js/shipyard.js takes a `balance` override: if `balance.shipGate` ever appears, it wins over everything below, field by field.

gate._versionDoc: Stamped into player.vehicles.shipyard when a character is made. A save with no stamp was made before the gate existed, so migrateSave() hands that character the Surveyor Lander and marks its four subsystems built — §9.19, nobody mid-run loses the ship they have been flying.

_subsystemDoc: Three tiers each, and a ship needs all four at its own tier. `signature` is the refined material that subsystem is mostly made of and no other subsystem uses — that is §9.5, and it is what stops one furnace and one recipe being the whole industry.

hull.name: Hull
hull.desc: Frame, skin and the seals between them. It is what keeps the outside outside.

drive.name: Drive
drive.desc: The engine and the tiles that stop it cooking everything else. The one piece that needs something the planet had to give you.

tanks.name: Tanks
tanks.desc: Where the fuel sits and, more to the point, stays. A tank that leaks is a short flight.
tanks._capacityDoc: Units of Drive Fuel the ship can hold at each tier. A lander's tanks hold three launches; deep tanks hold a tour.

avionics.name: Avionics
avionics.desc: How the ship knows which way is up, where the pad is, and how far it is to the next world.

warp.name: Warp Coil
warp.desc: §9.15: a coil, not a ship. Without it you fly between the worlds of one star; with it you leave the star.
warp._coreDoc: The coil's core has to come from a DIFFERENT family than the drive's, and a planet's one or two rare elements almost never span two families — so this is the piece that makes you go somewhere else for it, which is exactly what §9.6 asks for.

_coreDoc: The rare element goes into a CHARGED CORE, and there are four ways to make one — one per family of element. Every rare element in universe/data/elements.json belongs to exactly one family, so whatever the world under your feet happens to hold, there is a core you can build from it. That is the design decision: the gate must never hard-lock on a seed. tests/shipyard.test.js reads elements.json and fails if a new element is ever added to it without a home here.

core_arcane.name: Arcane Core
core_arcane.desc: A violet charge that will not sit still. The steadiest of the four and the hardest to find.

core_thermal.name: Thermal Core
core_thermal.desc: It burns from the inside and you build the tile around it before you touch it.

core_electric.name: Voltaic Core
core_electric.desc: A cell wound round a streak of storm-metal. Loud, bright, and perfectly reliable.

core_grown.name: Grown Core
core_grown.desc: Metal laid down by something alive. It is warm to hold and nobody enjoys that.

_shipDoc: §9.11: the three hulls that used to be shop stock are buildable tiers now. `needs` is the tier each subsystem must be at; `assembly` is what it costs to put them together on the pad.
_fuelDoc: §9.7 and §9.10: fuel is a consumable and it is per FLIGHT, not per launch, so the industry stays relevant after the first time the sky opens. Units of Drive Fuel (data/workshop.json), multiplied by the ship's own row above.

fuel._reserveDoc: A launch is refused unless there is enough left over to put the ship down again. Stranding a player in orbit with a dry tank is a loss they cannot undo, and that is not a difficulty setting, it is a bug.

_padDoc: §9.8: the pad is a structure, and the terrain tools exist so that you can make the ground flat enough for it. js/build.js owns placing it; these are the numbers it should read.

pad.name: Launch Pad
pad.desc: A levelled apron of cut block with a burn ring in the middle. It is also where the ship comes back to (§9.13).

_stationDoc: §9.15 and the far end of the ladder: an orbital yard. Four modules, each one a tier-3 craft that has to be LAUNCHED into orbit, which means a hauler, a pad and a lot of fuel. Finished, it refuels a ship without a synthesiser on the ground, it is a pad you can return to from anywhere in the system, and it is where an interstellar run is fitted out. It is a stated goal with stated requirements rather than a second game — everything it needs already exists in this file.

modules.name: Spine and Airlock
modules.desc: A corridor with a door at each end. Everything else bolts to it.

modules.name: Habitat Ring
modules.desc: Somewhere to sleep that is not a seat. It is also the only window in the system.

modules.name: Ship Cradle
modules.desc: Clamps, a fuel arm and a crane. A ship parked here is repaired and fuelled without ever landing.

modules.name: Power Array
modules.desc: Panels and batteries. Nothing above works without it, so it is the one people build first and the one this list puts last.

grants.desc: Refuel in orbit, return to it from anywhere in the system, and fit the warp coil without a refinery on the ground.

_marketDoc: §9.18: skipping is possible and it is meant to hurt. A city — not a village, not a camp — will sell a finished subsystem or a charged core at a price that assumes you are desperate. Buying is never cheaper than building, and the point of it is that a bad seed can never wall a player in.

market._fuelPriceDoc: Per unit of Drive Fuel, so a launch bought over the counter is about 1,600 gold. Enough to get home once; not a way to live.
